items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: I used to go up on Alpha's job when he was at the California, when I was working with him.

ctx.x: No, no, they don't know what we're talking about.

We always say that. Yeah, the cats get Shorty, they blow it out a bottle, ya know. Yeah, they don't know who Shorty is. Yeah, and they drink it, you know, and food will just think they can play better. Like I used to be weak to that effect. Oh, you get a little shorty, man, you can really blow. That's right, make you believe it. Yeah, and man, you'll be playing loud and raw. I used to go up on Alpha's job when he was at the California, when I was working with him. See, that's after the Lewis's Cafe. I worked with…

He come there and he always got smart. And the white people sitting right in the front, you know. Very insulted when they're drinking. Well, they didn't mad, you know. So he say, come there, George keep a worried me. The boss quite naturally going to worry me. Where is this one? Where is that one? I say, man, we don't all stay together. He know this is his job. He been here three years or four years or two years. He know he's supposed to be here. Keep asking me where is he at. I know where he at. I say, we all…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I had one guy. He came out in 46, Bob Watts. What did he play? Trumpet.

ctx.x: You have any New Orleans guys out there with you? No.

I had one guy. He came out in 46, Bob Watts. What did he play? Trumpet. Most of the time I had a mixed band. Some of the time I had white Mexicans. On the last I had, nobody was in the band. But me, I had four Mexicans with myself for about three years until my job closed.
What kind of music did the Mexicans play? My kind of music. College music. American music. They were, man. They were, man.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: I was surprised when I went out from Texas and seen him out there.

ctx.x: I don't know who Bob played with around here. He left early, you know. He left while I was playing on the roof guard around twenty-seven, twenty-six to twenty-seven. I was surprised when I went out from Texas and seen him out there. Because I didn't get out there until thirty-six. He said he left New Orleans around twenty-six. Used to work at Morris' Music Shop, you know.
